name: Intractable Diarrhea of Infancy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Intractable Diarrhea of Infancy

criteria.description: Persistent, severe diarrhea starting within the first months of life lasting more than 2 weeks despite standard treatment
Failure to thrive or poor weight gain despite adequate nutritional support
Exclusion of infectious, allergic, and metabolic causes of diarrhea through appropriate testing
Characteristic histopathological findings on intestinal biopsy (e.g., villous atrophy, epithelial abnormalities)
Identification of causative mutations in known genes associated with congenital diarrheal disorders

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Persistent severe diarrhea with failure to thrive and exclusion of infectious/metabolic causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires multidisciplinary evaluation including gastroenterology, pathology, and genetics.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe watery diarrhea persisting beyond neonatal period
searchTerms: severe watery diarrhea beyond newborn period

pathognomonic.symptomName: Failure to thrive despite adequate caloric intake
searchTerms: growth delay with normal food intake

pathognomonic.symptomName: Electrolyte imbalance secondary to chronic diarrhea
searchTerms: electrolyte problems caused by ongoing diarrhea
salt and mineral imbalance from diarrhea
blood chemistry changes due to diarrhea

common.symptomName: Dehydration signs (dry mucous membranes, decreased skin turgor)

searchTerms: mild low red blood cells from poor absorption
low blood count due to malabsorption
heart rhythm issues from electrolyte disturbances
immune deficiency due to poor nutrition

laboratory: Malabsorption markers (low serum albumin, vitamin deficiencies)
imaging: Abdominal ultrasound may show bowel wall thickening
Radiographs may show dilated bowel loops
genetic: Mutations in genes such as EPCAM, MYO5B, or other genes associated with congenital diarrheal disorders
other: Histopathology showing villous atrophy, epithelial abnormalities, or inflammatory infiltrates on intestinal biopsy

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of microvillus inclusions on electron microscopy
Severe congenital diarrhea with characteristic ultrastructural findings

redFlags: Persistent severe diarrhea unresponsive to standard therapies
Failure to thrive despite adequate nutritional support
Signs of severe dehydration or electrolyte imbalance
references: Orphanet: Intractable Diarrhea of Infancy - ORPHA:73014
Goulet O, Ruemmele F. Causes and management of intestinal failure in children. Gastroenterology. 2006.
